evidence.quote: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative for text generation, distinguished by their native support for parallel decoding.
Most recent diffusion LLMs follow the discrete masked diffusion model framework ( Shi et al., 2025 ; Sahoo et al., 2024 ) , formulating generation as an iterative unmasking procedure.
dLLMs begin with a largely masked sequence and gradually fill in masked positions over multiple denoising steps until all [MASK] tokens are resolved.
At each step, the model produces token distributions for the currently masked positions conditioned on the partially decoded sequence.
The confidence threshold for parallel decoding is 0.9, according to the widely used official setting.
DSB maintains an active block (red) that slides and can change its size across denoising steps, enabling globally causal yet locally parallel decoding.

we propose Dynamic Sliding Block (DSB) , a training-free block scheduling method that uses a sliding block with a dynamic size to overcome the rigidity of the naive block.
